name: Greater Accra
blurb: Ghana's national capital and economic heartbeat, home of the Independence Arch and the coastal Ga heartland.

name: Central Region
blurb: Historic Cape Coast and Elmina castles, the Kakum rainforest canopy, and the Effutu deer-hunting tradition.

name: Western Region
blurb: Ghana's oil and mineral coast, home of the stilt village of Nzulezo and lush rainforests.

name: Western North
blurb: Cocoa country and gold-rich forests of the Sefwi people in western Ghana.

name: Ashanti Region
blurb: The royal heartland of the Asante Kingdom, famed for the Manhyia Palace and Bonwire kente weaving.

name: Eastern Region
blurb: The green garden region of Aburi, twin Boti waterfalls, and the Krobo Dipo puberty rites.

name: Volta Region
blurb: The Ewe heartland of the Anlo people — monkey sanctuaries, Wli waterfall, Mount Afadjato and Mount Gemi.

name: Oti Region
blurb: A northern-Volta borderland along Lake Volta, home of the Nkonya people.

name: Bono Region
blurb: The historic Bono (Brong) kingdom of Techiman, land of the Apoo festival.

name: Bono East
blurb: Home of the Boabeng-Fiema monkey sanctuary and Lake Volta's northern catchments.

name: Ahafo Region
blurb: Forest-rich cocoa and timber lands of the Akan people, home of the Adekyem festival.

name: Savannah Region
blurb: Northern savannah grasslands home of Mole National Park and the Larabanga Ancient Mosque.

name: Northern Region
blurb: The Dagbon kingdom of Tamale, grandest stage of the Damba horse-and-drum festival.

name: North East
blurb: The Mamprusi heartland, gateway to the Gambaga escarpment.

name: Upper West
blurb: The far northwest, known for the Wa Naa palace and the Gologo harvest festival.

name: Upper East
blurb: The far northeast of dry savannah and sacred Paga crocodiles, famed for Bolga baskets.
